title: Fuel — Centre Tank Boost Pump Canisters — Bonding Lead Installation and Inlet Screen Change
abstract: Installation of dedicated bonding leads on the centre tank boost pump canisters and replacement of the fine inlet screen by a coarser item, closing a fuel system safety finding and removing the periodic bonding resistance check.

sections.planning_reason: A fuel system safety review found that the bonding resistance between the centre tank boost pump canister and the tank structure exceeded the design limit on 62 of 210 sampled aircraft, caused by corrosion of the canister mounting flange under the original sealant. A periodic bonding resistance check was imposed as an interim measure and is still in force on unmodified aircraft. Operators also report nuisance low fuel pressure warnings during centre tank transfer, traced to partial blockage of the fine inlet screen by sealant debris.
sections.description: This Service Bulletin fits each centre tank boost pump canister with a dedicated bonding lead terminated on the tank structure, renews the mounting clamp with an unsealed and bare faying surface inside a controlled area, and replaces the fine inlet screen by a coarser item that passes debris up to 0.8 millimetres while retaining the particle size the pump requires.
sections.accomplishment_summary: Defuel and purge the centre tank and confirm the atmosphere before entry. Open the tank access panels in zones 531, 631 and 114. Remove the pump canisters and measure the bonding resistance before disturbing anything, then record it. Remove the sealant from the mounting flange and clean the faying surface to bare metal inside the controlled area. Install the renewed clamp D2820008967217 and the bonding lead, terminated with the self-locking nuts EN968165-23. Measure the bonding resistance and confirm it is below five milliohms. Replace the fine inlet screen with the coarse item carried on the restrictor housing D2820003250655 and fit the captive retention nuts AGS15973-37. Re-install the canisters and do the pump operational test and the transfer test. Close the access panels, refuel and record the embodiment.
sections.effectivity_note: Applicable to all ZEPHYR-18, ZEPHYR-20, ZEPHYR-22 and ZEPHYR-24 aircraft of the classic models that are not already at the improved bonding standard. Aircraft delivered after the production cut-in have the bonding lead fitted at build and are not affected. The periodic bonding resistance check is deleted once this bulletin is embodied.
sections.material_note: Kit K2820-1163-01 contains the bonding leads, the clamps, the coarse screens and the captive nuts for one aircraft. Lead time is twelve weeks. Tank entry, purge and ventilation dominate the elapsed time; the mechanical work itself is under a shift.

type_data.compliance_time: At the next scheduled centre tank inspection, or within 48 months after the date of this Service Bulletin, whichever occurs first.
